newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO LOWERS HEAVY FUEL OIL PRICES ABOUT 8.28 PCT.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO LOWERS HEAVY FUEL OIL PRICES ABOUT 8.28 PCT.

text.p: Mexico lowered its heavy fuel oil prices by an average 8.28 percent at its six top refineries, effective on Friday, state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said late Thursday.
Pemex said in a statement that the adjustment was in line with lower international fuel oil prices.

Prices fell 7.76 percent to 766.46 pesos per cubic metre at the Cadereyta refinery, 10.58 percent to 715.48 pesos at Madero, 7.39 percent to 769.96 pesos at Minatitlan, 8.49 percent to 755.66 pesos at Salamanca and Tula and 7.19 percent to 786.01 pesos at Salina Cruz.
Heavy fuel oil prices also fell at shipping ports by a similar percentage, Pemex said.

"These movements in the Gulf of Mexico and the Pacific Coast reflect the behavior of external fuel oil markets and consider explicitly the differences in quality of the product in each of the system's refineries," it added.
Mexico's fuel oil is punitively priced because of its high sulfur content, analysts have said.
